# Example relational model — the single source of truth for PK/FK/identity
# (ADR 0032). Copy this file, rename it, edit it: nothing else declares
# relationships, and no `bq update` / `terraform apply` is involved.
#
# Names here are ALIASES on purpose. Real table/column names must never be
# committed (see config/relationships/README.md): drop your real model next
# to this file (the folder is gitignored apart from the examples) or pass
# --relationships_uri=gs://... at launch.

model: example_retail
description: accounts -> orders -> order lines, plus an unrelated ledger

tables:

  # A parent: no FK edges, so it generates first.
  A_TABLE:
    pk: [A_COL_001, A_COL_002]      # composite PK is fine
    identity: [A_COL_009]           # unique-but-not-key columns
    note: account master

  # A child: every row takes a WHOLE key tuple that A_TABLE landed
  # (ADR 0031), so orphans are impossible by construction.
  B_TABLE:
    pk: [B_COL_001]
    fk:
      - cols:     [B_COL_006, B_COL_007]
        ref:      A_TABLE                  # bare name = a table in THIS model
        ref_cols: [A_COL_001, A_COL_002]   # need NOT be the parent's full PK

  C_TABLE:
    pk: [C_COL_001]
    fk:
      - cols:     [C_COL_004]
        ref:      B_TABLE
        ref_cols: [B_COL_001]

      # A relationship that is real in the business model but whose join
      # key is not in the DDL: drawn in the card and the diagram, never a
      # source of keys.
      - cols:     [JOIN_KEY]
        ref:      A_TABLE
        ref_cols: [JOIN_KEY]
        enforced: false
        note: reporting-only link, key not materialised

  # Flip to false to DETACH this table: it stops travelling with the model,
  # and anything that reached the rest only through it detaches too. It
  # still generates when you target it explicitly.
  D_TABLE:
    enabled: false
    pk: [D_COL_001]
    fk:
      - cols:     [D_COL_002]
        ref:      C_TABLE
        ref_cols: [C_COL_001]

  # A parent OUTSIDE this model (already landed by another run) is
  # referenced dataset-qualified and needs no entry of its own.
  E_TABLE:
    pk: [E_COL_001]
    fk:
      - cols:     [E_COL_002]
        ref:      warehouse_ds.EXT_TABLE
        ref_cols: [EXT_ID]

# Example relational model — the two MULTI-PARENT shapes (ADR 0037).
#
# `example_*.yaml` files are DOCUMENTATION: a directory scan skips them
# (`relationships_example_skipped` in the launcher log), so a real model
# next to this file may reuse the same generic names. To load this one on
# purpose, point --relationships_uri at the FILE:
#
#   uv run --no-sync python3 scripts/relationships/card.py \
#     --relationships-uri config/relationships/example_star_diamond.yaml --all
#
# Names here are generic on purpose — real table/column names are never
# committed (see README.md § "Real names stay out of git").
#
# Two shapes in one model, deliberately disconnected:
#
#   star      dim_a ←── fact ──→ dim_b        (no ancestry between the dims)
#   diamond     top ←── left ←── bottom ──→ right ──→ top

model: example_star_diamond
description: a star-schema fact and a true diamond — the two ADR 0037 shapes

tables:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- star
  # Two independent dimensions. Neither descends from the other, so the
  # driving rule falls through to step 4 (ruling A): the FIRST DECLARED
  # enforced edge of `fact` drives, and the launcher logs
  # `fk_driving_edge_defaulted` (WARNING). Add `drives: true` to the edge
  # you want if the default is not the one you meant.

  dim_a:
    pk: [A_KEY]
    note: dimension — a root, generated first

  dim_b:
    pk: [B_KEY]
    note: dimension — a second root, unrelated to dim_a

  fact:
    pk: [A_KEY, B_KEY, LINE_NO]     # per-(A,B) line number completes the PK
    fk:
      # DRIVING (first declared, ruling A): `fact` rows are generated FROM
      # dim_a's landed keys — one request stream, one key tuple per child
      # (ADR 0036).  Card tag:
      #   [enforced, DRIVES (first declared — mark drives: true to choose)]
      - cols:     [A_KEY]
        ref:      dim_a
        ref_cols: [A_KEY]
        note: the parent whose keys drive generation

      # INDEPENDENT: shares NO column with the driving edge, so it keeps
      # the ADR 0030/0031 side-input key pool — a whole dim_b key tuple is
      # drawn per row, and the fk.orphan gate measures it.
      #   [enforced, independent]
      - cols:     [B_KEY]
        ref:      dim_b
        ref_cols: [B_KEY]
        note: a star-schema dimension — drawn from the sampled key pool

  # ------------------------------------------------------------- diamond
  # `bottom` reaches `top` twice: once through `left`, once through
  # `right`. Both branches carry T, so T must be ONE value that satisfies
  # both parents — that is what a conditional edge buys.

  top:
    pk: [T]
    note: the shared ancestor of both branches

  left:
    pk: [T, L]
    fk:
      - cols:     [T]
        ref:      top
        ref_cols: [T]

  right:
    pk: [T, R]
    fk:
      - cols:     [T]
        ref:      top
        ref_cols: [T]

  bottom:
    pk: [T, L, R]
    fk:
      # DRIVING: bottom is generated from left's landed (T, L) tuples, so
      # T and L are inherited from the key — never sampled.
      #   [enforced, DRIVES]
      - cols:     [T, L]
        ref:      left
        ref_cols: [T, L]
        drives:   true

      # CONDITIONAL on (T): shares T with the driving edge and adds R.
      # T comes from the driving key; R is one candidate that exists in
      # `right` FOR that T, picked from a co-partitioned CoGroupByKey on T
      # (Top-M per shared value, M = --fk_candidate_cap, default 64).
      #   [enforced, conditional on (T)]
      # If `right` holds no row for a T: R = NULL when R is NULLABLE in
      # the landing schema, else the key is dropped before generation and
      # reported as `fk.unmatched` (ruling B).
      - cols:     [T, R]
        ref:      right
        ref_cols: [T, R]
        note: the diamond's other branch — conditional on the shared T

# Public foreign-key example (ADR 0040) over the fictitious e-commerce dataset
# `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce`. The Dataflow Solution Guides
# deployment launches with it, from gcloud (`scripts/04_run_dataflow.sh`) or
# from Terraform (`launch_job = true`):
#
#   users ──< orders ──< order_items >── products (catalog, already landed)
#
# Terraform snapshots users, orders and order_items into `synthetic_source`
# with their exact public schemas, pre-creates the landing tables in
# `synthetic_data` with the same names and schemas, and copies `products`
# into `synthetic_data` as the parent that `order_items.product_id` draws
# from. A launch that targets order_items generates the whole component:
# users (num_rows), then orders from the users' landed keys, then
# order_items from the orders' landed keys.
#
# Files named `*_example.yaml` are samples: a directory scan skips them, so
# this model joins only a launch that names it with --relationships_uri.
model: gcp_public_thelook
description: users -> orders -> order_items, product_id from the landed products catalog

tables:

  users:
    pk: [id]
    identity: [id]          # fresh per-row keys; a sampled numeric PK would collide
    note: root, generated with num_rows rows

  orders:
    pk: [order_id]
    identity: [order_id]
    fk:
      - cols:     [user_id]
        ref:      users
        ref_cols: [id]

  order_items:
    pk: [id]
    identity: [id]
    fk:
      # Driving edge widened with user_id, so every item copies the user of
      # its order instead of drawing one (ADR 0036).
      - cols:     [order_id, user_id]
        ref:      orders
        ref_cols: [order_id, user_id]
        drives:   true
      # Implied: orders already carries user_id from users.
      - cols:     [user_id]
        ref:      users
        ref_cols: [id]
      # External: the catalog is not generated; keys are drawn from the
      # landing dataset's products table.
      - cols:     [product_id]
        ref:      synthetic_data.products
        ref_cols: [id]

model: invented_widening
tables:
  G:
    pk: [G1, G2]
  P:
    pk: [PG1]
    fk:
      - cols: [PG1]
        ref: G
        ref_cols: [G1]
  C:
    pk: [CG]
    fk:
      - cols: [CG]
        ref: P
        ref_cols: [PG2]
        drives: true
      - cols: [CG]
        ref: G
        ref_cols: [G2]

description: a star-schema fact and a true diamond — the two ADR 0037 shapes

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- star

  # driving rule falls through to step 4 (ruling A): the FIRST DECLARED

    pk: [A_KEY]

  dim_b:
    pk: [B_KEY]
    note: dimension — a second root, unrelated to dim_a

  fact:

      #   [enforced, independent]

  # ------------------------------------------------------------- diamond
  # `bottom` reaches `top` twice: once through `left`, once through
  # `right`. Both branches carry T, so T must be ONE value that satisfies
  # both parents — that is what a conditional edge buys.

    pk: [T]
    note: the shared ancestor of both branches

  left:
    pk: [T, L]
    fk:
      - cols:     [T]
        ref:      top
        ref_cols: [T]

  right:
    pk: [T, R]
    fk:
      - cols:     [T]
        ref:      top
        ref_cols: [T]

  bottom:
    pk: [T, L, R]
    fk:
      # DRIVING: bottom is generated from left's landed (T, L) tuples, so
      # T and L are inherited from the key — never sampled.
      #   [enforced, DRIVES]

        ref_cols: [T, L]

      # T comes from the driving key; R is one candidate that exists in
      # `right` FOR that T, picked from a co-partitioned CoGroupByKey on T

      # the landing schema, else the key is dropped before generation and
      # reported as `fk.unmatched` (ruling B).

        ref:      right
        ref_cols: [T, R]
        note: the diamond's other branch — conditional on the shared T
